issues.legal_issue: Disputes concerning obligations expressly reserved for court enforcement by the agreement are excluded from its arbitration clause.
material_facts: The agreement provided that disputes concerning obligations identified in specified clauses could be specifically enforced through a court.
The arbitration clause applied to disputes arising out of or relating to the agreement, except for the matters covered by the court-enforcement provision.
The parties disagreed about whether the claims raised fell within that exception; the Supreme Court did not determine whether the actual claims did.
issues.conclusion: A dispute concerning the obligations covered by the express court-enforcement provision is not arbitrable under the agreement; whether the claims in this case concerned those obligations remained for the High Court to examine.
issues.legal_principle: The agreement must be interpreted according to its terms, without rewriting it, and an arbitration clause is construed strictly. An express exception to arbitration must be given effect. The Court relied on Sections 7 and 11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, and Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Narbheram Power and Steel (P) Ltd., Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation v. Diamond and Gem Development Corporation Ltd., Harsha Construction v. Union of India, and Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation.

predicates.section_eleven_reference: A party asks a court to refer a dispute to arbitration or appoint an arbitrator under the statutory reference procedure.
predicates.express_court_enforcement_exception: The parties' agreement expressly reserves specified disputes for enforcement through a court rather than arbitration.
predicates.dispute_concerns_excepted_obligations: The dispute concerns obligations that the agreement reserves for court enforcement.

issues.definition: When a party seeks a court reference, an express court-enforcement exception applies, and the dispute concerns the excepted obligations, the dispute is excluded from arbitration.

issues.legal_issue: A court considering an application to appoint an arbitrator must conduct a preliminary review when a specific objection asserts that the dispute falls within an express contractual exception to arbitration.
material_facts: The applicants sought appointment of arbitrators under the agreement's arbitration clause.
The opposing party specifically contended that the dispute fell within the agreement's court-enforcement exception and was therefore not arbitrable.
The High Court appointed arbitrators without first deciding whether the dispute fell within that exception.
The Supreme Court set aside the appointment and remitted the application for a preliminary inquiry into arbitrability and the scope of the exception.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was required to conduct a preliminary inquiry into whether the dispute fell within the contractual exception and was arbitrable. Its appointment order was set aside, and the application was remitted for that inquiry.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11(5) and (6) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, judicial review at the reference stage is limited and prima facie, not a mini-trial. The court may intervene where non-arbitrability is manifest and ex facie certain, and it must address a specific plea that the dispute is covered by an express exception rather than appointing arbitrators without inquiry. The Court relied on Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation and Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. v. NCC Ltd.; it also referred to Uttarakhand Purv Sainik Kalyan Nigam Ltd. v. Northern Coal Field Ltd.

predicates.section_eleven_appointment_proceeding: A party has applied to a court for appointment of an arbitrator under the statutory appointment procedure.
predicates.specific_exception_objection: A party specifically contends that the dispute falls within an express contractual exception to arbitration.
predicates.appointment_without_preliminary_review: The court appoints arbitrators without first making a preliminary assessment of whether the dispute falls within the asserted exception.

issues.definition: In an appointment proceeding, when a specific contractual-exception objection is raised and the court appoints arbitrators without preliminary review, the appointment is set aside and the matter is remitted for that review.
